translation_direction: ru → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Russian electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Pushkin’s lean, brisk, ironic memoir prose is kept without ornament; Pugachev’s rough warmth, Savelich’s old-servant speech and the proverbs are rendered with Vietnamese equivalents.
decisions.rationale: The economy of the style is the point.

decisions.decision: The Russian text comes from Wikisource’s page of the 1978 Nauka edition; editorial notes and page numbers were removed, and the omitted chapter kept as a final section.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: The father’s counsel ‘кому присягнешь’ was garbled into ‘the son who swore’; now ‘người mà con đã tuyên thệ trung thành’.
‘Я его хозяйка’ (I am his wife) was rendered as ‘landlady’; now ‘tôi là vợ ông ấy’.

Grinev’s rhymed love poem in the stilted Trediakovsky manner was rendered as unrhymed neutral verse, which left Shvabrin’s mockery unmotivated; now three rhymed ABAB quatrains in an archaic, over-sweet register (checked by a narrower review after the fix).
‘Казацкие старшины’ was rendered ‘già làng’; now ‘các thủ lĩnh Cô-dắc’.
Pugachev was called ‘hắn’ in the tender farewell; now ‘ông ta’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: Не приведи бог видеть русский бунт
glossary.draft_rendering: Xin Chúa chớ cho thấy một cuộc nổi loạn của Nga — vô nghĩa và tàn bạo, không chút xót thương
glossary.rationale: The famous line, kept in one wording.
Cossack officers or elders, not village elders.
‘Hắn’ only in the mouths of those who despise him.

witness_decision: Selected the Russian Wikisource transcription of Капитанская дочка (1836) based on the 1978 Nauka edition (Pushkin, Polnoe sobranie sochinenij v 10 tomakh, vol. 6, pp. 258–370, via az.lib.ru); the project did not collate it with the first printing in Sovremennik.

unresolved_questions.explanation: ‘Междуусобие’ is rendered ‘cuộc xích mích trong nhà’, which understates the mock-heroic word.
The last two rhymes of the poem reuse the syllable ‘ơi’ and the last line runs long.
‘Самолюбивый’ is rendered ‘tự ái’ (touchy) rather than vain.

title_review.rationale: The title is rendered as ‘Con gái viên đại úy’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: Grinev’s account of his father, a retired premier-major in Simbirsk.
The last unit: the narrator’s incomplete closing note on the pardon and the story’s end.
